content.text:
**Scope note.** I audit seven programmes. Six sit inside the "dark matter is stuff" frame; one denies it. Note also a framing point that matters for the ranking: *collisionless cold dark matter as an effective description* is a distinct programme from any particular candidate, and it is in far better shape than any of its candidate-level children. My 2026-dated coverage is thin (search budget exhausted mid-way), so treat the last ~6 months as provisional.

---

## 1. CDM as effective paradigm (ΛCDM's gravitational core)

**Status.** The claim audited here is minimal: dark matter is non-baryonic, cold (negligible thermal velocity at decoupling), effectively collisionless, ~5× baryon density. This is what fits CMB acoustic peaks (Planck 2018), BAO, the Lyman-α forest, weak-lensing surveys (DES Y3, KiDS, HSC; Euclid now delivering), cluster lensing offsets in mergers (Clowe et al., *ApJ* 2006, Bullet Cluster), and the abundance of Milky Way satellites (DES/Pan-STARRS satellite censuses). Open sores: small-scale structure — core/cusp, diversity of rotation curves, "too big to fail" (reviewed by Bullock & Boylan-Kolchin, *ARA&A* 2017) — plus the S8 and (less relevantly) H0 tensions, and JWST's surprisingly bright high-z galaxies. Crucially it says nothing about *what* the stuff is, which is why it survives every null result from particle searches.

**Axis 1 (diachronic): progressive.** Genuine corroborated novel predictions across three decades (peak structure, BAO scale, lensing-mass/light offsets, satellite counts at predicted amplitudes); small-scale fixes are mostly baryonic-feedback modelling rather than modifications of the dark sector.
**Axis 2 (synchronic): strong.** Maximal unifying power from two numbers (Ωc, cold), high consistency with GR and nucleosynthesis; the weak virtue is fertility *about the constituent*, which it deliberately brackets.
**Axis 3 (social): healthy but with lock-in risk.** Large, competitive, multi-collaboration, with blinded analyses and public pipelines; concentration of authority in a handful of simulation suites (IllustrisTNG, FIRE, EAGLE) and the reflex of attributing small-scale residuals to feedback is a real invisible-degeneration channel.
**Axis 4 (formalisation): excellent triangulation.** Convergence crosses instrument families (CMB radiometry, optical imaging, X-ray, spectroscopy), disciplines, and auxiliary hypotheses; only (c) the GR frame is shared, which is exactly what programme 7 attacks.
**Axis 5 (teleological): both readings positive.** It accumulates true quantitative knowledge (Bird) and organises structure formation into one story (Dellsén) — while conceding the constituent question.
**Stanford meta: satisfied at this level** — the main rival (modified gravity) is formulated and tested against it.

**Verdict: solid.** **Pathology:** none.
*Charitable defence against a harsher verdict:* none needed; the honest attack is that "cold and collisionless" is so thin it is nearly unfalsifiable — but that is answered by the specific small-scale predictions it does make.

---

## 2. Axions and axion-like / wave-like bosons

**Status.** The QCD axion is the only candidate motivated by an independent problem — strong CP (Peccei–Quinn 1977; Weinberg, Wilczek 1978) — with cosmological production built in (Preskill, Wise & Wilczek 1983). Haloscope coverage is real but narrow: ADMX reports a search from 1.10–1.31 GHz (≈4.6–5.4 µeV) at extended-KSVZ sensitivity (ADMX Collaboration, arXiv:2504.07279, 2025), with HAYSTAC, CAPP/IBS, ORGAN, MADMAX, DMRadio, ABRACADABRA/SHAFT and CASPEr pushing other decades; ALPS II (DESY) and the planned IAXO attack couplings model-independently. The frontier is now diversifying into new signal channels — e.g. a first search exploiting Earth-matter screening/gradient enhancement with an alkali–noble-gas comagnetometer (KEK-QUP, arXiv:2602.20260, 2026). The ultralight "fuzzy" branch (Hu, Barkana & Gruzinov 2000) is being squeezed from below by Lyman-α and dwarf-galaxy dynamics, so its original selling point — fixing small-scale structure — is largely gone.

**Axis 1 (diachronic): progressive but slow.** No detection, yet the programme has not changed shape to absorb nulls: post-inflationary scenarios *predicted* the tens-to-hundreds-of-µeV window before experiments reached it, and lattice topological-susceptibility calculations narrowed it independently.
**Axis 2 (synchronic): high.** Solves two problems with one field (unifying power), simple, and extremely fertile — it keeps generating new detection concepts rather than new excuses.
**Axis 3 (social): good.** Many small independent groups rather than one mega-collaboration, so no single point of failure; conversely, small-team analyses have a thinner replication record and candidate signals (stellar-cooling hints, TeV transparency) have historically been over-read.
**Axis 4 (formalisation): genuinely independent routes.** Cavities, LC circuits, NMR/spin precession, helioscopes, light-shining-through-walls, plus astrophysical bounds from neutron-star cooling and NuSTAR — different instruments, different couplings, different auxiliaries; the shared element is the QCD-axion frame itself.
**Axis 5 (teleological): noetic strength ahead of epistemic.** It organises understanding (CP, DM, inflationary cosmology) far better than it currently accumulates facts — a large parameter space is still untouched.
**Stanford meta: partially satisfied.** The "axion" label now covers a sprawl of ALPs, which quietly protects the programme from refutation by any single null result.

**Verdict: defensible with reservations.** **Pathology:** none primary; watch **untestability creep** in the ALP-sprawl branch.
*Charitable defence:* even the pessimistic reading concedes that the theoretically favoured mass window will be swept by the 2030s — this is a programme with a decisive test scheduled, not deferred.

---

## 3. WIMPs / weak-scale thermal relics

**Status.** The flagship programme of 1985–2015, now under severe pressure. Xenon TPCs have improved spin-independent sensitivity by orders of magnitude with no signal: LZ's latest analysis uses 417 live days (March 2023–April 2025) and finds no WIMPs in the 3–9 GeV range while setting world-leading low-mass limits (LZ Collaboration, 2025; earlier record limits published in *Phys. Rev. Lett.*, 2025), and XENONnT's inference machinery is documented in *Phys. Rev. D* 111, 103040 (2025). Both LZ and XENONnT/PandaX now see solar-neutrino coherent scattering — the "neutrino fog" — meaning the era of cheap sensitivity gains is ending; next-generation XLZD/DARWIN/PandaX-xT, DarkSide-20k and SuperCDMS are the last big pushes. The LHC has found no mediators, and DAMA/LIBRA's annual modulation has been contradicted by ANAIS-112 and COSINE-100 using the same target material. The community response has been to migrate to sub-GeV, freeze-in, and hidden-sector candidates.

**Axis 1 (diachronic): degenerating.** The one sharp prediction — a relic at the electroweak-scale cross-section, ideally supersymmetric — is dead over most of its natural range, and the last decade's moves (coannihilation corners, blind spots, split/stealth SUSY, then wholesale relabelling as "hidden sector") rescue different anomalies-of-absence without a common gain.
**Axis 2 (synchronic): virtues eroding.** Empirical accuracy is fine (nulls are consistent), but unifying power collapsed with the failure of naturalness-driven SUSY, and simplicity is gone once each null requires a dedicated model corner.
**Axis 3 (social): best-in-class error correction.** Blinded analyses, salting, direct experiment-vs-experiment confrontation with the same target (ANAIS/COSINE vs DAMA), published likelihoods — the programme's honesty about its own nulls is exemplary and argues against lock-in.
**Axis 4 (formalisation): triangulation attempted, all channels null.** Direct detection, colliders, and indirect searches (Fermi-LAT dwarfs, AMS-02, IceCube) are properly independent across instruments and auxiliaries; convergence is on absence, which is informative.
**Axis 5 (teleological): epistemic yes, noetic no.** It has produced enormous reliable knowledge — a map of what dark matter is *not* — while its promised understanding (DM as a by-product of solving the hierarchy problem) has not materialised.
**Stanford meta: now well satisfied** — mostly because the programme's own failure forced the rivals into existence.

**Verdict: fragile.** **Principal pathology: ad-hocness** (secondary: **overfit** — a dedicated model region per exclusion contour).
*Charitable defence:* "WIMP" was always a class, not a model, and the class extends to any thermal relic from keV to 100 TeV; sensitivity to it has improved ~10⁶× in 25 years, which is progress by any instrumental standard, and the remaining unexplored range down to the neutrino floor is where several well-motivated models live.

---

## 4. Self-interacting dark matter and structured dark sectors

**Status.** The most vigorous astrophysics-driven programme. It takes the small-scale anomalies as signal rather than noise and adds a light mediator. Current calibration: cluster scales (v ~ 1000 km/s) require σ/m ≲ 0.1–1 cm²/g while galactic-scale rotation curves of low-surface-brightness and ultra-diffuse galaxies want σ/m ≳ 3 cm²/g, forcing a strongly velocity-dependent cross-section, which also produces both cored halos at high mass and gravothermal core *collapse* at low mass (see the SIDM Concerto simulation compilation and data release, *ApJ*, 2025, and references therein to Kaplinghat et al. 2016, Nadler et al. 2023, Yang et al. 2023). Its live discriminating targets are the diversity of rotation curves at fixed mass, dark-matter-deficient galaxies, and anomalously compact strong-lens perturbers.

**Axis 1 (diachronic): progressive, contested.** It made a genuine novel prediction — enhanced *scatter* in halo densities at fixed mass, and collapsed ultra-dense subhalos — and evidence for both has appeared; the velocity dependence, however, was introduced to reconcile cluster and galaxy scales, so partly accommodative.
**Axis 2 (synchronic): mixed.** Good fertility and empirical reach on small scales, but simplicity is sacrificed (a mediator mass, a coupling, a velocity profile) and it must contend with baryonic feedback (FIRE, NIHAO) explaining the same data with no new physics.
**Axis 3 (social): open but degeneracy-prone.** Active simulation community with public data releases (a real error-correction asset), yet astrophysical systematics — inclination, non-circular motions, feedback prescriptions — leave much room for undetected bias, and the field's key comparisons rarely take the form of blinded tests.
**Axis 4 (formalisation): weak independence.** Rotation curves, stellar kinematics, strong lensing and cluster shapes are different observations but overwhelmingly share the same auxiliary hypotheses (halo modelling, baryonic feedback prescriptions) and the same discipline; no laboratory route exists.
**Axis 5 (teleological): noetic gain.** It converts a list of unrelated small-scale puzzles into one parameter, which is genuine understanding-organisation even before any detection.
**Stanford meta: strongly satisfied** — SIDM lives in explicit competition with feedback-CDM, WDM and MOND on the same datasets.

**Verdict: defensible with reservations.** **Pathology:** none primary; **mono-method** is the standing risk.
*Charitable defence:* velocity-dependent cross-sections are not a patch but a generic consequence of light-mediator dark sectors written down before the cluster/galaxy tension was quantified.

---

## 5. Primordial black holes

**Status.** The only programme requiring no new particles. Windows are heavily constrained: CMB accretion (Planck), Subaru-HSC and OGLE microlensing, dwarf-galaxy survival, and LIGO/Virgo subsolar-mass merger searches leave roughly the asteroid-mass range (~10¹⁷–10²³ g) as the surviving region for PBHs as *all* of DM, and light-PBH bounds keep tightening — e.g. from Hawking-radiation heating of the intergalactic medium reconstructed from Lyman-α forest thermal broadening over 12 Gyr (*Phys. Rev. D* 112, 123019, 2025). Two recent live threads: the "memory burden" argument (Dvali and collaborators, 2024–) claiming that semiclassical evaporation halts, which would reopen sub-10¹⁵ g masses; and scalar-induced gravitational waves as a genuine forward test (PTA data, later LISA). PBHs are also routinely invoked *post hoc* for JWST's early massive galaxies and LIGO's heavy black holes.

**Axis 1 (diachronic): mixed, drifting toward degenerating.** It has a real predictive channel (induced GW background, specific mass-function shapes), but the pattern of the last decade — mass window closes, a new production mechanism or evaporation caveat reopens a different one — is the signature of accommodation.
**Axis 2 (synchronic): good simplicity, weak accuracy.** Ontologically minimal and consistent with GR, but it requires a tuned enhancement of the primordial power spectrum on a chosen scale, which imports the very fine-tuning it saves elsewhere.
**Axis 3 (social): fluid, moderately self-correcting.** Small community with rapid public back-and-forth on constraints; papers claiming PBH explanations for whatever anomaly is topical suggest publication incentives are pulling toward positive claims.
**Axis 4 (formalisation): genuinely strong triangulation — against it.** Constraints come from lensing surveys, CMB spectral/anisotropy data, X-ray/radio accretion, IGM thermometry and GW interferometry: four instrument families, different auxiliaries, mostly independent.
**Axis 5 (teleological): partial.** It illuminates the early-universe power spectrum regardless of whether PBHs are DM — arguably its most durable contribution.
**Stanford meta: satisfied,** the alternative-space is explicitly mapped in mass-fraction plots.

**Verdict: fragile.** **Principal pathology: ad-hocness.**
*Charitable defence:* PBHs are the only candidate whose existence requires no physics beyond GR plus inflation, so a non-zero PBH fraction is close to a prediction rather than a hypothesis; and the memory-burden reopening is a theoretical derivation, not a fitted patch.

## 6. MOND and the modified-gravity family

**Status.** Milgrom's 1983 modification remains unmatched at predicting galaxy-scale phenomenology — the baryonic Tully–Fisher relation and the radial acceleration relation (McGaugh, Lelli & Schombert, *PRL* 2016), rotation curves of gas-rich dwarfs from photometry alone, and external-field-effect signatures. Its failures are equally structural: galaxy clusters still need unseen mass, GW170817 killed the TeVeS-type variants via the photon–graviton speed difference, and relativistic completions that do fit CMB and matter power spectra (Skordis & Złośnik, *PRL* 2021, AeST) do so by adding fields whose stability and cluster behaviour remain contested. The current decisive battleground is wide binaries in Gaia DR3, where claims are directly contradictory: a MOND-type low-acceleration anomaly is reported as confirmed after reworking data-quality cuts and multiple-star modelling (arXiv:2607.14450, 2026, arguing that a contrary result by Cookson et al. 2026 rests on only 61 binaries in the MOND regime), against null results from Banik and collaborators. Unresolved as of this writing.

**Axis 1 (diachronic): the best novel-prediction record on galaxy scales, degenerating elsewhere.** Predictions made in 1983 were corroborated decades later on objects unknown at the time; but each move outward (clusters → sterile neutrinos or extra dark fluid; CMB → extra fields; lensing → new sector) is a separate rescue with no common gain.
**Axis 2 (synchronic): split.** Unrivalled accuracy-per-parameter within galaxies (one constant, a0), near-zero unifying power across cosmology, and consistency with the established corpus (GR, GW constraints) purchased only through added structure.
**Axis 3 (social): insular and polarised.** A small community with a strong shared prior, a limited number of gatekeeping venues, and a decade-long unresolved dispute between two or three groups over the same Gaia sample — precisely Zollman-style durable polarisation, with analysis-choice sensitivity (cuts, multiplicity modelling) that no blinded protocol currently arbitrates.
**Axis 4 (formalisation): mono-frame.** Its evidence is almost entirely galaxy kinematics from optical/radio spectroscopy interpreted through a dynamical-equilibrium auxiliary; the wide-binary test is valuable precisely because it would break that dependence, which is why its irreproducibility is so damaging.
**Axis 5 (teleological): noetic yes, epistemic doubtful.** MOND organises galaxy-scale regularities that CDM does not naturally explain — the a0 coincidence with cH0 is a real puzzle it forces on everyone — but it does not currently accumulate a consistent body of true claims across scales.
**Stanford meta: it *is* the unexplored alternative** that keeps the CDM programme honest; hybrid options (superfluid DM, Berezhiani & Khoury 2015; emergent gravity, Verlinde 2016) are formulated but largely stalled.

**Verdict: fragile.** **Principal pathology: mono-method** (secondary: **insularity**; the cluster/CMB patches also invite **ad-hocness**).
*Charitable defence:* strong and worth weighing — MOND's galaxy-scale predictions are novel in the strict Lakatosian sense and have never been *predicted* by CDM, only fitted after the fact by feedback tuning; a programme that keeps generating anomalies its rival must absorb is not in bad epistemic health, even if its cosmology fails.

## 7. keV sterile neutrinos / warm dark matter

**Status.** Attractive because the νMSM would deliver neutrino masses, the baryon asymmetry and dark matter at once (Asaka & Shaposhnikov and collaborators). Empirically it is nearly cornered: the 3.5 keV X-ray line, its main positive evidence, was excluded as decaying dark matter by blank-sky and halo analyses (Dessert, Rodd & Safdi, *Science* 2020; Foster et al. 2021); Lyman-α forest power spectra push the thermal-relic mass above roughly 5 keV, while X-ray non-detections cap the mixing angle from the other side, leaving only a sliver for resonant (Shi–Fuller) production. Laboratory reach is limited and slow (KATRIN/TRISTAN). Theoretical output continues briskly — e.g. keV sterile neutrino DM embedded in left–right symmetric models with modular flavour symmetry (Kakoti & Das, *PTEP* 2025, 123B12) — which is model-building against a shrinking target.
 
**Axis 1 (diachronic): stagnant-to-degenerating.** The falsifiable version made a checkable prediction (an X-ray decay line) and lost it; what remains are model-building variants that relocate the candidate without generating new corroborable predictions.
**Axis 2 (synchronic): unifying power without accuracy.** The νMSM's three-for-one economy is its great virtue; it is undercut by the fact that the surviving parameter space is a fine-tuned corner and that WDM's original motive — suppressing small-scale structure — is now largely excluded by Lyman-α and satellite counts.
**Axis 3 (social): thin but not pathological.** The X-ray-line episode was corrected in public by independent reanalysis, a good sign; the surviving activity is heavily weighted toward theory papers with little prospect of near-term test, a classic invisible-degeneration setting.
**Axis 4 (formalisation): good independence, negative result.** X-ray astronomy, Lyman-α spectroscopy, satellite counts and beta-decay spectroscopy are independent in instrument, discipline and auxiliaries — and they converge on exclusion.
**Axis 5 (teleological): modest.** Its lasting contribution is a sharpened link between neutrino-sector physics and cosmological structure, not knowledge of dark matter.
**Stanford meta: satisfied**, largely by the same X-ray data that killed the flagship signal.

**Verdict: fragile.** **Principal pathology: untestability** (the surviving window has no near-term decisive probe); secondary **invisible degeneration**.
*Charitable defence:* unlike WIMPs, sterile neutrinos are guaranteed-plausible physics — right-handed states are the simplest explanation of neutrino mass — so the programme's cost is low and a next-generation X-ray spectrometer (XRISM-class or Athena) could still find the line in the resonant window.

## Ranking — best to worst current shape

1. **CDM as effective paradigm** — the only programme with a corroborated novel-prediction record across four independent instrument families; its weakness (silence about the constituent) is also what makes it robust.
2. **Axions / wave-like bosons** — independent theoretical motivation, real and diversifying experimental routes, an unexplored but *bounded and scheduled* parameter space. Best-placed candidate-level programme.
3. **SIDM / structured dark sectors** — genuinely predicted the scatter and collapse signatures now being seen; downgraded for mono-method dependence on astrophysical modelling and for the feedback-CDM rival explaining the same data.
4. **WIMPs / thermal relics** — instrumentally magnificent, theoretically in retreat; its knowledge output is now mostly exclusionary, and the migration to "hidden sectors" is a change of programme, not a continuation.
5. **Primordial black holes** — a legitimate, minimal hypothesis whose decade-scale behaviour has been window-closing-followed-by-window-reopening; the induced-GW test is what could rescue it from ad-hocness.
6. **MOND family** — ranked low despite the *best* Axis-1 record of all, because Axes 3 and 4 are severely compromised and the cosmological failures are structural; the unresolved wide-binary dispute is currently the single highest-value experiment in this whole list.
7. **keV sterile neutrinos** — closest to outright refutation as the whole of dark matter, with no near-term decisive probe. Worst position, not for lack of rigour but for lack of remaining room.

**Global caveats.** *Strongest overall element:* the independence structure supporting CDM's gravitational core (Axis 4). *Weakest overall element:* every candidate-level programme is short on laboratory-vs-astrophysical triangulation — most rely on convergence within one instrument family or one auxiliary framework. *Worth checking further:* (i) the Gaia wide-binary analyses, ideally by a blinded, pre-registered third-party pipeline; (ii) whether the memory-burden claim survives independent derivation; (iii) whether SIDM's compact-perturber evidence survives lens-modelling systematics; (iv) my 2026 coverage, which is incomplete. *Charitable defence against this ranking as a whole:* it rewards breadth of corroboration and penalises boldness, so it systematically flatters the programme that predicts least (CDM's effective core) and punishes the one that predicted most on the scale where data are best (MOND) — a partisan of either MOND or PBHs can fairly say the apparatus is here measuring institutional consolidation as much as truth-tracking.
